note: The roster of major US companies across the 23 market industries of industries.json, 1947-2025. Who is in it: the companies Jev (TypeSafe System One) scored 2.0 or more on a five-level judgment of how major a player each was in its US industry at its peak (0 a minor firm, 2 among the larger dozen, 3 among the largest five, 4 the leader or co-leader; "major": true), and the 75 hand-picked companies of company-lives.json ("curated": true), chosen for famous rises and falls. Each stands in the industry Jev chose as the one earning most of its revenue at confidence 0.6 or more, else in the authored one ("judged" keeps Jev's answers: they are judgments, not measurements; Docs/research/companies/judgments.json has the full distributions). "value" is the year-end market value in nominal billions of dollars as [year, usdBn, kind, fact]: "m" a measured value, CompaniesMarketCap's end-of-year market capitalization (its history begins in 1996 or at listing; the current year and a delisted company's last, not-year-end value left out), each from a research fact the truth gate verified (the fact id, in Docs/research/companies/<cluster>.json); "a" an approximate recalled waypoint from company-lives.json (+-30-50%; for private companies a funding valuation), kept only before or after the measured span and never to be drawn as measured. Candidates were today's largest US companies of each industry and the historical giants that still traded after 1996; giants that left the market before (Gulf Oil, RCA, Pan Am's peers) have no measured value and appear only if curated. Built by Tools/companies/build.py.
